findings.failure_path: The gate is reached without a trigger. 'Small' has no definition and no upper bound, and the agent applies the label to its own run. The Stop reason, session-start.md and session-policy.md all say not to 'invent a cost cap'. An agent can label a large or repeated metered run a 'small test' and skip asking, because the user never set a limit. The probes cover only two calls with an account confirmed in advance, so nothing tests a run that is not small.
findings.smallest_fix: Give 'small' a concrete test, for example the cost stays within what the task already covers. Say that a run whose cost the agent cannot bound beforehand is a real blocker. Add a FAIL probe where the agent continues an open-ended or large metered run.

findings.failure_path: The agent decides on its own whether a change is 'backward-compatible'. It can label a breaking change to an API with external callers as compatible and merge without sign-off, since its own review counts. The only control (prd-human-high-impact) covers money/permission paths, not an API change wrongly described as compatible.
findings.smallest_fix: Require the compatibility call to rest on a reviewed interface diff, checked by the external reviewer, before the exemption applies. Add a FAIL probe: the external interface removes or renames a field, the agent calls it compatible, then continues to merge.

findings.failure_path: The acceptance criteria require actual validation results before a shared branch update. The evidence says the full make test lane and the R0-status harness are still pending, and the plan says review is pending. If the PR branch is updated now, the shared update happens before those results exist.
findings.smallest_fix: Do not push to the PR until the full make test run and the R0-status rerun finish. Record their actual outputs in the plan's evidence directory, then change the plan status.

concern_results.conclusion: I checked the Makefile split, the locale suite's runtime mutations, the hook's clause scoping, the liveness helper and the oracle rows; none fails in this diff. I agree with the prior dispositions on replicas, missing PIDs and preparation-only. Two failures remain. First, the agent alone decides whether a test counts as 'small' and whether an API change is 'breaking', and both decisions skip a gate. Second, the evidence still records the full make test lane as pending.

Explicit user count limits, destructive actions in dev, preparation-only scope and high-impact merge/launch each have a paired control. The gap is the agent's own judgment calls. No rule or test checks how 'small' is decided when the user set no cost limit. The new 'backward-compatible' exemption from sign-off is decided by the same agent the gate applies to, and no control probe covers a breaking change misdescribed as compatible.
